description:
FILED s452ab (Opus, round 11 agent AB) from the #721 probes.  PRE-EXISTING on
main 0dd7434 and untouched by #721 (that task fixed the RETURN VALUE of a list
assignment; this is the ASSIGNMENT itself).

A dereferenced array or hash inside a list-assignment LHS must absorb the
REST of the RHS, exactly as a plain `@a` / `%h` does.  PCL treats it as ONE
slot, so it gets one element (and, in the array case, that one element is
then discarded because p-setf writes through the cast, not into the array).

REPRO (perl vs ./runpcl, measured on 0dd7434 AND after #721):
    my $r = []; my $x;
    ($x, @$r) = (1,2,3);
    print "x=$x r=[@$r] n=", scalar(@$r), "\n";
        perl: x=1 r=[2 3] n=2
        PCL:  x=1 r=[] n=0            <-- SILENT WRONG

    my $hr = {}; my $y;
    ($y, %$hr) = (9, a=>1, b=>2);
        perl: y=9 h=[a=1,b=2]
        PCL:  y=9 h=[]                <-- SILENT WRONG

    my @l = ((@{[]}) = (1,2));        # the same rule with no leading scalar
        perl: 2 elements
        PCL:  1

WHERE: `p-list-=` in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp dispatches its LHS elements on the
FORM.  A bare `@arr` / `%h` SYMBOL takes the greedy arm (`(subseq src-vec
idx)` / the hash twin); a `(p-cast-@ â¦)` / `(p-cast-% â¦)` form is not a
symbol, so it falls into the generic `t` arm, which consumes exactly one slot
and does `(p-setf VAR one-value)`.  The fix is a third and fourth greedy arm
keyed on the CAST head â the greedy question is "is this target an
AGGREGATE", and the answer must not depend on whether the aggregate is named
or dereferenced (rule 11: one predicate, four spellings).  Note the LHS also
sets `greedy-done`, and the list-context collect (#721) must push the
aggregate's elements the same way the symbol arms do.

BAR: the three rows above vs perl in both contexts, plus `(@$r) = ()`
(clears), `($x, @$r, $z) = (1,2,3)` (perl starves $z), the postfix spellings
`$r->@*` / `$hr->%*` in an LHS list, and a `local` LHS; guard rows beside the
#721 family in Pl/t/aassign-01.t.
subject: a DEREFERENCED array/hash in a list-assignment LHS is not greedy: ($x, @$r) = (1,2,3) leaves @$r empty
